class: STREETS & TRAFFIC WAYS — formal + informal manmade traffic surfaces that push the natural landscape aside along the road network (street/alley spines), rendered as a paint-on-top surface pass over the existing 32x32 Wang terrain (per-tile surface.manmade flag + chunk-bake composite + edge, through GL). Maps formal carriageways onto street_spine and informal lanes/tracks onto alley_spine; the natural biome shows through under fill and kerb, so geometry is biome-agnostic and variation is a biomeSkins tint + climate overlay.

tierRecommendation: Sort by formality + asset-readiness, but per the maximal-by-default mandate NONE are deferred — all 14 ship. Tier A (formal, kerbed_wang, share the same 6-piece biome-agnostic kerb skeleton + per-type fill tile, claim AVAILABLE today via street_spine/district.kind): g_street_cobblestone, g_street_granite_setts, g_street_ashlar_road, g_street_brick_herringbone. These are the cheapest formal corpus (4 fill tiles + 1 shared kerb skeleton with palette skins). Tier B (informal, procedural_fringe = ZERO authored edge tiles, claim AVAILABLE today via alley_spine + wetness-driven selection): g_lane_rammed_earth (the baseline, mostly the biome dirt tile), g_lane_gravel, g_alley_back_lane, g_corduroy_log_road. Cheapest of all — no kerb corpus, fringe only. Tier C (formal EDGE/threshold features that REUSE Tier-A assets but NEED-DECLARING new spine-network nodes — gutters, crossings, intersections, gate aprons): g_street_gutter_kennel (declare gutter-run on formal kerb edges), g_crossing_stepping_stones (declare threshold/intersection nodes), g_tollgate_apron (declare gate/boundary threshold). Tier D (water crossings — NEED-DECLARING water_edge crossing claims, the highest-integration tier, touches hydrology + possibly the building system for arches/trestles): g_ford_stone_crossing, g_bridge_deck_stone, g_bridge_deck_timber. Build Tier A+B first (claims exist today, prove the paint-on-top + kerb-Wang + fringe machinery on the free claim sources), then Tier C (declare spine-network threshold/intersection/gutter nodes), then Tier D (declare water_edge crossings, integrate with hydrology/foam + bridge structure).
gaps: WATER_EDGE crossing claims are not emitted: spine geometry and hydrology water tiles both exist, but there is no claim at the tile where a spine crosses river/shallow_water, and no bridge-vs-ford-vs-causeway selection. Blocks g_ford_stone_crossing, g_bridge_deck_stone, g_bridge_deck_timber. Must DECLARE in layout.js (or a roads/hydrology join): per spine-segment, detect water-tile intersection and emit {crossing: 'ford'|'bridge_stone'|'bridge_timber'} keyed by spine.tier (street→stone bridge, alley→timber/ford) + watercourse width.

THRESHOLD / INTERSECTION nodes are not emitted: street_spine and alley_spine are independent polylines; their intersections (where streets cross) and their settlement-boundary endpoints are not computed as claim points. Blocks g_crossing_stepping_stones and g_tollgate_apron, and would improve cobble/sett junction treatment. Must DECLARE intersection points (spine-spine proximity) + boundary endpoints (spine reaches district edge / gate building_role) as threshold claims.

GUTTER/KENNEL edge-runnel role is not declared: the kerb line of a formal surface exists (it's the Wang edge), but there's no flag that a given kerb run carries a drainage channel. Blocks g_street_gutter_kennel. Must DECLARE a gutter-run as a derived sub-feature of formal-surface edges (cheap: it rides the existing kerb skeleton with 1-2 added channel pieces).

WETNESS is only a BINARY water predicate today (isWaterTile/buildingTouchesWater); there is no 0-1 wetness scalar wired (hydrology.js exists but is not integrated). This makes the puddle-when-wet and mud affordances, and the corduroy-vs-earth / ford-frequency selections, COARSE (on/off) rather than graded. Same gap the D-stack flagged. Wiring a wetness scalar would sharpen every traffic-way's wet/mud/puddle affordance.

PAVED-vs-UNPAVED selection rule for a given spine is not declared: the engine knows street_spine vs alley_spine and district.kind, but the mapping {which surface fill a spine gets} (cobble for civic street, brick for craft, gravel/earth for outer alley, corduroy for wet alley) must be authored as a deterministic selection table keyed on (spine.tier, district.kind, underlying biome/wetness). All inputs are sim-derived/AVAILABLE; only the mapping table is unauthored.

DECLARED PLAZAS/SQUARES (settlement open paved spaces) are out of this CLASS (they belong to a plazas/concourse class) but ADJOIN streets — the street surface needs to know to TERMINATE its kerb cleanly into a plaza rather than fringe to grass. Cross-class seam: NEEDS-DECLARING plaza regions so street kerbs resolve against them. Noted as a dependency, not a surface in this class.

BRIDGE/CAUSEWAY STRUCTURE (arches under a stone deck, trestle under a timber deck, the deck HEIGHT above water) is a building-system / GL-depth concern, not pure ground-paint. g_bridge_deck_stone and g_bridge_deck_timber author only the DECK SURFACE here; the supporting structure + over-water depth sorting must be declared as a building-system integration so the deck doesn't render as flat paint floating on water.

AGE / MAINTENANCE are honestly absent (no sim source), same as the D-stack. The wear-path/crack/missing-plank/polish affordances are therefore driven only by available co-drivers (traffic-density proxy = spine.tier + distance-to-center, wetness, biome climate-default, exposure/shade for alleys), NOT by true road age or upkeep. Surfaces never FAKE an age — heavier wear on busier spines is an honest traffic proxy, but graded decay over time stays dormant until a chronicle road-age/upkeep source lands.

class: CIVIC, PLAZA & CEREMONIAL (the public realm + ritual) — G-stack manmade-ground surface types. Paved/decorated outdoor surfaces of the PUBLIC and SACRED realm: the formal civic floor, the market and town square, the temple/palace forecourt, the processional way, the dais, the consecrated burial path, the sacred precinct, the monument setting. All render via the grounds paint-on-top pass over 32x32 Wang terrain (surface.manmade flag + chunk-bake composite through GL), seeded per-tile (wx,wy). These are the MOST FORMAL surfaces in the game and therefore lean kerbed_wang edges; nearly all sit on declared_plaza or district:civic/market claims, so the majority are NEEDS-DECLARING (plazas/squares/precincts are not yet emitted by layout.js — only district.kind=civic|market and road spines exist today).

surfaceTypes.fill: Large irregular-but-fitted flagstone slabs (ashlar-leaning), tight mortar joints, broom-swept clean reading; the default public-square floor. Cool grey biome-tinted stone with subtle slab-to-slab tonal variation for a hand-laid look (not a repeating grid).
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_plaza
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (declared_plaza polygon at civic district centre) — the central civic-district circle EXISTS (district.kind='civic', innermost radius ~0.25*maxRadius, anchored town_hall/courthouse in layout.js generateDistricts), but a PLAZA/SQUARE region is NOT emitted.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL only (geometry biome-agnostic): grassland/forest=cool grey granite flag; desert/savanna=warm sandstone; volcanic=dark basalt; beach=coral-block; tundra/arctic/taiga=grey flag with snow-cover overlay default; swamp/river=damp green-grey moss-joint default; mystic=faint rune-veined flag (emissive multiplier, no cast light). Natural biome shows in the fringe seams.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (desire-line polish on the town_hall<->road crossing), cracks (older tiers), moss-joints (mortar lines, default-on in damp), puddle-wet (rain in worn dishing, GL specular), snow (cold overlay)
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 flagstone FILL tile (32x32) + shared ~6-piece biome-agnostic kerb Wang skeleton (fill/straight/outer-corner/inner-corner/end-cap/strip, rotated to 16 masks). Native 32px per Wang-32 rule.
surfaceTypes.notes: The class baseline; default fill the other civic types inherit. Formal => kerbed edge framing the square against lawn/road. Joint+wear+puddle ride the SAME D0-D2 dressing coverage mechanics on the ground plane.

surfaceTypes.label: Market square paving (cobble setts)
surfaceTypes.fill: Coursed cobble setts / small squared pavers in fan or running-bond — a hard-wearing trade floor built to take cart wheels and crowds. Rougher and warmer than civic flagstone; visible cart-rut polish down the trading lanes.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:market
surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today (claim) — district.kind='market' EXISTS (anchored shop/bazaar). The market district polygon is usable now; a tighter declared_square at the market centre is NEEDS-DECLARING for the crisp kerbed square (procedural_fringe against the district edge works today).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: grassland=grey-tan cobble; desert=pale sandstone setts; volcanic=basalt; beach=worn beach-stone; cold=snow overlay (cleared paths=wear-path snow-melt); swamp=algae-green damp; mystic=rune-fleck. Geometry shared.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (heavy — cart-ruts + stall-front polish, strongest wear of any civic surface), worn (rounded sett crowns), puddle-wet (rut hollows), moss-joints (between setts), cracks (sunken setts), snow
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 cobble-sett FILL tile (32x32 biome-tinted) + shared kerb skeleton; pairs with procedural_fringe where market bleeds into informal ground. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Working formality (labouring trade floor, not ceremonial). edgeStyle BOTH: kerbed at a declared square edge, fringe where it dissolves into the street/alley net. Distinct from civic flagstone by pattern (setts vs flags) + heaviest cart-rut wear.

surfaceTypes.label: Grand concourse / temple-palace forecourt
surfaceTypes.fill: Monumental ashlar paving — large precisely-cut rectangular slabs in a grand regular bond with a central axial band of contrasting stone leading to the building's main door. Forecourt of a temple/palace/town hall/great civic anchor; the grandest, cleanest floor in the public realm.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: building_role:civic_anchor
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (forecourt apron keyed off the civic-anchor building door+frontage) — the ANCHOR exists (district.anchor='town_hall'|'courthouse'|'bazaar'; specialization.id for temple/shrine) but the forecourt region is not emitted.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: marble-white/cream high-status temperate; warm limestone desert; polished basalt volcanic; per-biome wall-material echo so it reads as belonging to its building. Cold=snow overlay (axial band cleared=>wear-path). Mystic=luminous inlay band (emissive).
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (axial approach band to the great door polishes brightest), puddle-wet (shallow sheet on flat slabs, strong GL specular for the grand reflective look), cracks (sparse, well-maintained), moss-joints (edges only), snow
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 ashlar FILL + 1 axial-band STRIP variant (contrasting stone to the door, reuses the kerb 'strip' piece recoloured) + shared kerb skeleton. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: High-status sibling of the civic plaza — larger regular slabs + directional axial band aimed at the anchor door. Always kerbed (most formal possible edge). Sits in front of exactly the civic/temple/palace anchor buildings the district system names.

surfaceTypes.label: Processional way (ceremonial avenue)
surfaceTypes.fill: A broad LINEAR ceremonial paved avenue — wide flagstone/ashlar with a strong directional central spine line and flanking kerbs, connecting a gate/road to a temple, shrine, monument or civic anchor. Reads as a route, not a field: paving laid ALONG the axis.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: street_spine
surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today (spine geometry + 'paved' flora-suppression delta) / NEEDS-DECLARING (ceremonial tag) — road SPINES exist as waypoint polylines tagged tier='street' (generateRoadSpines). The processional distinction (a spine promoted to ceremonial because it links a gate to a temple/civic anchor) must be DECLARED as a spine tag.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: grand light stone like the forecourt; per-biome stone family; cold=snow overlay with cleared centre (wear-path); mystic=glowing inlaid centre-line (emissive). Geometry shared, laid along a polyline.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (strong central desire-line down the avenue), puddle-wet (linear pooling along crown/gutter), cracks, moss-joints (flanking kerb line), snow
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: Reuses the forecourt ashlar FILL + axial STRIP, but the engine lays it along a street_spine polyline (linear) with kerbs both sides. No new fill tile; +1 optional centre-line marker strip. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: The LINEAR ceremonial member (vs FIELD members like plaza/forecourt). Distinct claim source (a tagged road spine) — exactly where the existing street-spine polyline + paved-suppression delta become a no-mock anchor. Kerbed (formal avenue with raised flanking kerbs).

surfaceTypes.label: Mosaic / patterned ceremonial floor
surfaceTypes.fill: An ornate patterned/mosaic inlaid floor — geometric or figurative tessellation (rosette, knotwork, star, labyrinth) set into the centre of a temple forecourt, shrine precinct or civic rotunda. The most decorated ground surface in the game; a small high-status inlay panel, not a whole square.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_plaza
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a declared inlay-centre sub-region inside a declared_plaza or temple forecourt) — no sim source emits a 'mosaic centre'; declare as the centroid feature of a civic/temple plaza claim.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: tesserae palette per culture/biome (temperate=red/cream/black geometric; desert=blue/gold arabesque; mystic=constellation mosaic emissive; volcanic=obsidian-and-ash; cold=snow overlay PARTIALLY occluding the pattern). Pattern GEOMETRY is shared art; only the palette tints.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (rosette centre polishes where people stand/cross), cracks (missing tesserae => honest decay), moss-joints (inter-tessera grout in damp), puddle-wet (sheen lifting the colours), snow (partial-cover overlay)

surfaceTypes.label: Monumental steps & terrace
surfaceTypes.fill: Broad shallow ceremonial stair runs and stepped terraces — the tiered approach up to a temple, town hall, monument or raised precinct. Reads as parallel tread-and-riser bands (a stacked-step ground texture) framed by heavy kerb cheek-walls, with landings of plain ashlar.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: building_role:civic_anchor
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a stepped-terrace region + its rise, in front of a raised civic/temple anchor) — building anchor roles exist; the REGION and an elevation delta the steps span must be declared. Honest dependency: meaningful steps want a height delta the ground engine can read.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: light monumental stone matching the forecourt; per-biome stone family; cold=snow on the treads (wear-path=cleared centre); mystic=glowing riser edge-lines (emissive); volcanic=basalt. Step GEOMETRY shared; tint only.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (tread-nosing polish down the centre line), cracks (worn step noses chip => honest age), moss-joints (damp risers in shade), puddle-wet (water sheeting on treads/landings), snow (tread cover, centre cleared)
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: A tread/riser band TILE set (step-run fill + landing + the kerb cheek-wall pieces, ~4-5 tiles, 32x32) — the only civic surface whose 'fill' is a directional banded step texture rather than a flat paver. Kerb skeleton supplies the cheek-walls. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: The vertical-transition member. Carries an honest height dependency (steps without a rise are a lie) — flag it. Directional banded fill (treads run perpendicular to the climb axis). Always kerbed (cheek-walls are structural kerbs).

surfaceTypes.label: Fountain / well-head surround
surfaceTypes.fill: The paved apron and basin-kerb encircling a public fountain, ornamental basin, or grand civic well-head at a square's centre — radial/concentric paving stepping out from the basin rim, with a raised circular kerb holding the water edge.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_plaza
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a fountain point-feature at a plaza/square centroid) — no sim source places public fountains. The D6 well prop exists as a private-yard analogue, but the public fountain + paved surround is new and ground-class.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: light stone basin-kerb + radial apron per biome stone family; the WATER surface uses the existing GL water-reflection pass (no own sprite); cold=frozen-basin overlay (ice tint) + snow apron; desert=adobe/sandstone basin, water default 'low'; mystic=glowing rune-rim. Geometry shared.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (the gather-ring where people draw water / sit on the basin kerb), puddle-wet (splash-zone always wet, strong GL sheen around the rim — wettest civic surface by definition), moss-joints (damp grout near the basin, default-on), cracks (older basin kerb), snow/frozen overlay
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 radial-apron FILL variant (concentric paving) + a circular basin-KERB ring (reuses outer/inner-corner kerb pieces curved) + shared kerb skeleton for the outer apron. Basin water rides the GL water pass. ~3-4 tiles, native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Defined by permanent splash-wetness (puddle-wet is the default ground state, not a rain affordance). A focal centrepiece surround inside a plaza fill. Always kerbed (the basin rim IS a kerb). Reuses GL water-reflection rather than authoring water art.

surfaceTypes.label: Civic dais / speaking platform
surfaceTypes.fill: A raised paved platform — the speaking dais, proclamation stage, market-cross base, or judgement-seat plinth at a square's focal point. Plain dressed ashlar top framed by a raised kerb-edge plinth; small footprint, deliberately elevated above the surrounding plaza.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_plaza
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a focal dais point-feature at a civic-square centroid, often where district.anchor='town_hall'/'courthouse' faces the square) — declare the dais claim; honest minor height dependency (the raise) like the steps.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: dressed ashlar top + plinth kerb per biome stone family; cold=snow on the platform top; mystic=glowing rune-edged plinth; volcanic=basalt. Geometry shared.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (centre-of-platform speaker polish + the step-up edge), cracks (plinth corners chip), moss-joints (shaded plinth base), puddle-wet (flat top sheets in rain), snow
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 platform-top FILL (plain ashlar) + the raised plinth KERB ring (reuses kerb corner/straight pieces as a low retaining edge). ~2-3 tiles, native 32px. Frequently pairs with g_monumental_steps_terrace for the step-up.
surfaceTypes.notes: The 'stage' of the public realm — small, raised, focal. Differs from the plaza fill by being an ELEVATED kerb-bounded island within the square. Honest height-raise dependency flagged alongside the steps. Often co-placed with a market-cross/monument prop (a separate D6-style object, not this ground).

surfaceTypes.label: Consecrated / graveyard path
surfaceTypes.fill: The kerbed gravel-and-slab walk threading a churchyard / burial ground / shrine grounds — a quiet narrow consecrated route between grave plots, paved in modest slabs or bound gravel with a low kerb edge. Solemn, well-kept-but-aged reading.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:civic
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a graveyard/consecrated-ground sub-region — a civic sub-district or a region beside a temple/shrine building_role) — no cemetery in layout.js. Path geometry can ride a declared internal spine once the burial region exists.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: muted grey slab / pale bound gravel per biome; damp biomes (swamp/river/dense_forest)=moss-joints + lichen default (solemn overgrown reading); cold=snow overlay; mystic=faintly glowing memorial inlay; desert=pale sand-gravel. Geometry shared.
surfaceTypes.affordances: moss-joints (DEFAULT-ON — the defining solemn-overgrown look), wear-paths (gentle, the tending-route between plots), cracks (heaved old slabs), worn (rounded gravel-bound surface), puddle-wet, snow
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 modest-slab/gravel FILL tile + shared kerb skeleton (low kerb). Distinguished by leaning hard on moss-joints + worn affordances rather than new geometry. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: The funerary/consecrated member — formal but quiet, defined by default moss/lichen overgrowth (honest age expressed through affordance coverage, since the age sim-driver is absent we lean the climate/damp default). Narrow linear path inside a declared burial/shrine region.

surfaceTypes.label: Sacred circle / ritual precinct
surfaceTypes.fill: A consecrated ground ring — a stone-ringed or ground-marked ritual precinct (standing-stone circle floor, shrine clearing, ley-marked ground, druidic/temple-grove precinct). Often NOT fully paved: marked/cleared sacred ground with a stone perimeter ring rather than a hard floor, so natural biome shows strongly through.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_region
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a sacred precinct / ritual site as a declared special region, could anchor off a temple/shrine building_role or a standalone declared POI) — no sim source places ritual sites.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: perimeter ring stone + ground-marks per biome (grassland=worn earth ring + standing stones; desert=sand-ring + cairn; forest/dense_forest=mossy grove-ring; volcanic=obsidian ring; mystic=GLOWING rune-circle ground inlay, the strongest emissive overlay in the class; cold=snow-dusted ring). The natural biome is intentionally the dominant under-layer.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (the trodden ritual-circle path, the central gathering ring), moss-joints (perimeter stones in damp), worn (bare trodden sacred earth), puddle-wet, snow; cracks only on the stone ring
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: A perimeter stone-ring KERB variant (the marked edge) + an optional faint ground-mark FILL (rune/earth-ring inlay, sparse — much of the interior is bare biome). Uses procedural_fringe heavily so natural ground dominates; kerbed only on the stone ring. ~2-3 tiles, native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: The least-paved, most natural-dominant member — a SACRED-GROUND claim more than a paved floor (honest absence of full paving is the point). edgeStyle BOTH: a hard kerbed stone ring with a procedural fringe interior. Mystic biome makes this the showpiece glowing rune-circle.

surfaceTypes.label: War-memorial / monument paving
surfaceTypes.fill: The solemn paved setting around a monument, war memorial, cenotaph, or honour-stone — a small formal precinct of dark dressed stone with a contrasting frame band, set within or beside a civic square. Dignified, kept clean, a place of standing not of traffic.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_plaza
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (a memorial point-feature with a paved setting at a civic-square edge or its own small precinct) — no sim source emits memorials/monuments. History/chronicle could later anchor WHICH event it commemorates — honestly absent now.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: TINT+MATERIAL: dark dignified stone (slate/basalt/dark granite) with a contrasting pale frame band per biome; cold=snow overlay (centre kept cleared); mystic=memorial inlay glows faintly; desert=dark-on-pale sandstone. Geometry shared.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (the standing/laying-tribute ring close to the monument base), puddle-wet (flat dark stone sheets, very reflective — strong GL sheen), cracks (sparse, kept-maintained), moss-joints (frame edges in damp), snow
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 dark dressed-stone FILL + 1 contrasting frame STRIP (reuses the kerb strip piece) + shared kerb skeleton. ~2-3 tiles, native 32px. The monument itself is a separate D6-style prop; this is only its paved ground setting.
surfaceTypes.notes: The commemorative member — a dark formal frame-banded precinct around a monument prop. Honest content-absence: WHICH event/person it memorialises wants a chronicle/history source that is absent (the paved setting renders regardless, generically). Distinguished from the dais by being a place to stand AT (low traffic, dark reflective stone) not a stage to stand ON.

tierRecommendation: Sort by formality x claim-readiness, but NONE are deferred (the user asked for maximal-and-complete-by-default; all 12 ship). TIER A (build first — claim source AVAILABLE today): g_market_square_paving (district.kind='market' live) and g_processional_way (street spines + 'paved' flora-suppression delta live) — these two can render against today's sim data with procedural_fringe immediately, no new declarations, proving the G-stack on real claims the way the D0 pilot proved the D-stack. TIER B (core public realm — one shared declared_plaza primitive unlocks the lot): g_civic_flagstone_plaza, g_grand_concourse_forecourt, g_fountain_surround, g_civic_dais_platform, g_war_memorial_paving — all just need the single new declared_plaza region (plus civic-anchor forecourt) emitted in layout.js; they then share ONE flagstone/ashlar fill + the ~6-piece kerb skeleton, so marginal cost per type after the first is tiny (a tint + an affordance lean + maybe one feature tile). TIER C (decorated/ceremonial features — authored panels or honest extra dependencies): g_mosaic_ceremonial_floor (authored inlay panel set), g_monumental_steps_terrace + the g_civic_dais_platform raise (honest HEIGHT dependency the ground engine must read), g_consecrated_path + g_sacred_circle_precinct (need a declared burial/ritual region). Asset economics overall: ~6 shared kerb pieces + ~6-8 distinct fill/feature tiles cover ALL 12 types across ALL 21 biomes (biomeSkins = tint + climate overlay, never new geometry) — consistent with the PLAN's ~12-tiles-not-2000 budget.
gaps: declared_plaza / declared_square is the single biggest gap: layout.js generateDistricts emits the CIVIC district (innermost circle, town_hall/courthouse anchor) and the MARKET district, plus road spines, but NO plaza/square/forecourt polygon. 7 of 12 types (flagstone plaza, forecourt, mosaic, fountain, dais, war-memorial, and the precise market square) are blocked on declaring this one region primitive. The PLAN already flags this as NEEDS-DECLARING.

Processional/ceremonial SPINE TAG: road spines exist (tier='street'|'alley', waypoint polylines via generateRoadSpines) but there is no flag promoting a spine to ceremonial because it links a gate to a temple/civic anchor. g_processional_way needs that one boolean tag (or a derive rule: street spine whose endpoint is a civic/temple anchor).

HEIGHT / elevation for steps & dais: g_monumental_steps_terrace and the g_civic_dais_platform raise are honestly compromised without a rise the ground engine can read (steps with no height delta are a lie). Needs either a foundation/terrain height delta exposed to the grounds paint pass or a declared platform-height attribute.

Consecrated & ritual REGIONS: no cemetery/graveyard and no ritual/sacred-site sub-region are emitted by layout.js. g_consecrated_path and g_sacred_circle_precinct need a declared burial region and a declared ritual-site region (could anchor off temple/shrine specialization once those roles are confirmed in specializations.js).

AGE driver honestly absent (PLAN.md confirms): cracks/heaved-slabs/missing-tesserae/worn-nosings all WANT an age signal with no sim source. We lean on the available co-drivers (wetness, biome damp/cold climate-default, traffic-derived wear-paths) and the tier glyph; true age-graded decay stays dormant until a maintenance/age source exists.

MAINTENANCE / wealth driver absent: civic surfaces split sharply by upkeep (a swept marble forecourt vs a moss-choked neglected square). With maintenance/wealth honestly absent, tidiness is placed by default per type (high-status types lean clean, consecrated leans overgrown) rather than driven — flagged so it can wire later.

Per-tile WETNESS scalar still binary: puddle-wet and the fountain splash-zone want the 0-1 wetness scalar the PLAN notes is unbuilt (terrain-suitability exposes only binary water predicates; hydrology.js not integrated). Puddle affordances run on rain-state + proximity heuristics until the scalar is wired.

MONUMENT / fountain PROPS are separate objects: this class authors only the GROUND settings; the actual fountain basin sculpture, market-cross, monument, standing stones and memorial stone are D6-style ground PROPS that must be co-placed at the same declared centroids. The ground claim and the prop placement need to share the declared-feature point so they don't drift apart.

Commemorative CONTENT absent: g_war_memorial_paving renders generically because WHICH event/person it honours wants a chronicle/history source (absent). Honest: the paved setting exists, the specific dedication does not — no faked inscriptions.

Plaza/precinct vs flora-claim coexistence: these surfaces must suppress F0-F8 flora across whole multi-tile regions (the PLAN notes the roads-sim 'paved' suppression delta as the model). A declared_plaza needs to emit the same paved-suppression so trees/decoration don't punch through the civic floor — that region-scale suppression is only wired for road spines today, not for declared regions.

surfaceTypes.label: Worn-earth desire-line path
surfaceTypes.fill: bare trodden topsoil — biome dirt with the flora scoured off down to packed soil; faint braided central rut darker/smoother than the feathered margins; per-tile noise breaks it into a meandering organic ribbon, never a ruler-straight band
surfaceTypes.claimSource: alley_spine (street spine tagged alley → narrow informal way) PLUS desire-line tracing between building_role:<any> door thresholds and the nearest street_spine; the roads-sim already emits a 'paved'/trodden flora-suppression delta along these polylines — we reuse that suppression mask as the claim, painting trodden earth where flora was pushed aside. AVAILABLE-today.
surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: tint only over the natural biome dirt showing through: grassland=loam-brown; forest/dense_forest=dark humus + needle-fleck; desert/savanna/steppe=pale dust-tan, fringe is sand-feather not grass-feather; swamp/river/lake=dark wet-clay, raise puddle-wet baseline; arctic/tundra/taiga=path reads as packed snow-grey with frozen ruts (see snow-trodden variant), suppress green fringe; volcanic=ash-grey trodden cinder cast; mystic=faint cool-luminous trodden line. surfaceTypes.label: Packed-earth cart/foot track
surfaceTypes.fill: compacted graded earth, firmer and flatter than a raw desire line — a deliberately maintained working track; subtle paired wheel-ruts where it carries cart traffic, a low crowned centre, occasional dried-mud ridge at the margins

surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: grassland=mid clay-brown crowned track; desert/steppe/savanna=hard-pan pale, wind-rippled margins; swamp/river=darker, ruts default puddle-wet; forest=root-crossed humus track; arctic/tundra=frozen rutted ground reading grey-white; volcanic=packed ash track. Tint+climate overlay only, shared fringe geometry.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (cart ruts), worn, mud (wet-weather/wet-biome rut softening), puddle-wet (ruts pool), snow (winter cover), cracks (sun-baked hard-pan crazing in arid biomes)
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: ZERO authored edge tiles; procedural fringe. Fill = procedural packed-earth bake at 32px native with an optional paired-rut overlay mask (per-tile, driven by role traffic weight). No kerb.
surfaceTypes.notes: The 'busier than a desire line, not yet paved' tier. Honest-absence: where the roads-sim later upgrades a spine to 'paved' this surface yields to the formal street/cobble class — paths never pretend to be streets.

surfaceTypes.label: Loose gravel / pea-shingle path
surfaceTypes.fill: loose small-stone gravel scatter — speckled mid-tone aggregate with per-tile stone-noise so no two tiles tile-repeat obviously; slightly sunken centre where feet have pressed the gravel into a shallow trough; thin gravel-spill feather at the edge rather than a hard kerb
surfaceTypes.claimSource: desire-line/approach from building_role:<manor|inn|temple|townhouse|civic> door thresholds to the street_spine (gravel = a tidier informal approach a wealthier household lays down); declared_region:garden interior paths once garden regions are declared. Door-approach + role are AVAILABLE-today; the garden-region host is NEEDS-DECLARING.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (garden-region interior runs need a declared_region:garden in layout.js; the door→street approach run is AVAILABLE-today)
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: grassland/hills=grey-tan flint pea-gravel; desert=warm sandstone chips; forest=darker basalt chips + leaf-litter speckle; arctic/tundra=frost-greyed gravel, snow settles between stones; volcanic=black scoria gravel; mystic=pale opal chips with faint glint. Tint + grain-palette swap, shared fringe.
surfaceTypes.affordances: worn (centre trough), puddle-wet (gravel darkens, shallow surface sheen when wet — no deep pooling), snow (settles between stones, partial cover), moss-joints (damp/shaded biomes grow moss between gravel — reuses the joint-moss affordance even without authored joints, applied as low-coverage speckle), mud N/A (gravel resists mud)

No kerb in the informal form; an OPTIONAL shared kerb-Wang edge may be declared if a formal gravel court is wanted (then it borrows the biome-agnostic ~6-piece kerb skeleton).

tierRecommendation: Sort by formality and asset-readiness, but ALL are included (nothing deferred), matching the maximal-by-default directive. TIER 1 (informal, procedural-fringe, ZERO authored edge tiles, claim AVAILABLE-today): g_path_worn_earth_desire_line, g_path_packed_earth_track, g_path_cinder_ash, g_path_sand, g_path_snow_trodden. These are pure procedural surface-override/overlay bakes over the live Wang ground reusing the roads-sim flora-suppression delta and door->street desire lines, so they ship first with the proven D-stack-mechanism-A paint-on-top path and the shared procedural fringe; no new corpus at all. TIER 2 (small authored raised-element sets, claim AVAILABLE-today, place-on-top NOT surface-override -- needed for honest wet/soft ground): g_path_stepping_stone, g_path_duckboard_plank, g_path_log_corduroy. Each needs only a tiny shared slab/board/log decal set (2-5 pieces, no Wang skeleton) and lets the natural wet ground show through -- the honest answer over water/bog. TIER 3 (informal/working, procedural-fringe, but host region NEEDS-DECLARING in layout.js): g_path_gravel (garden interior), g_path_woodchip_bark (garden/orchard), g_path_herb_garden (bed grid). Their door-approach runs are available today; their interior-garden runs unlock once declared_region:garden exists. TIER 4 (formal, edgeStyle 'both' -> share the biome-agnostic ~6-piece kerb Wang skeleton with the STREETS/PLAZA class, partly NEEDS-DECLARING): g_path_flagstone_garden, g_path_paved_pebble_setts. These straddle into the paved-surface family and reuse the formal class's kerb corpus, so they are authored alongside that class, not duplicated. Across all four tiers exactly TWO shared kerb-skeleton dependencies and THREE tiny raised-element sets are the only authored geometry; everything else is procedural over the live biome.
gaps: declared_region:garden / kitchen-garden bed-grid does NOT exist in layout.js yet -- gravel, wood-chip, herb-garden, flagstone-garden, and pebble-sett interior runs are NEEDS-DECLARING and currently can only claim their door->street APPROACH segment, not the garden interior. The sim emits district.kind and building roles but no per-garden region with bed geometry.
declared_plaza / declared concourse not in layout.js -- the formal flagstone/pebble approach-FRINGE around plazas has no host until plazas are declared (flagged in the plan's NEEDS-DECLARING list).

No continuous WETNESS scalar (terrain-suitability exposes only BINARY water predicates; hydrology.js not integrated). So puddle-wet, mud, and damp-board affordances run on a binary near-water flag + season, not a true 0-1 wetness field -- the wet-ground choice between solid paving vs stepping-stone vs duckboard is heuristic, not driven by a real soil-saturation value.

AGE / MAINTENANCE honestly absent (no chronicle wires them) -- wear-path intensity, rut depth, board rot, joint-moss maturity, and centre-polish all currently key off available co-drivers (traffic weight from role, exposure, biome climate-default) at a fixed baseline rather than accumulated path age. A brand-new path and a century-old one look identical until age is wired.

WEALTH honestly absent -- WHO upgrades a desire line to gravel / flagstone / pebble-sett (vs leaving bare earth) is gated only by role-anchor PROXIES (manor/temple/inn/guildhall) the sim emits, not by a real household wealth value. Formal path types may appear at the right buildings but cannot yet vary by actual prosperity.

Desire-line TRACER not confirmed in code -- the plan confirms the roads-sim emits 'paved'/trodden flora-suppression deltas along street/alley SPINES (polylines), and door positions exist, but an explicit building-door -> nearest-spine desire-line path TRACE (and building->building informal traces) is NOT confirmed to be emitted today. The alley_spine claim is available now; the pure door-approach desire line for many path types may need a small tracer built on the existing spine + door data.

Raised-element placement (stepping-stone slabs, duckboards, corduroy logs) is a DIFFERENT mechanism from the surface-override paint pass: it is on-top decal/sprite placement that must let the live Wang ground render between/under elements. The G-stack design currently specs the surface-override paint pass and the kerb-Wang/fringe edge; it does NOT yet spec this 'place-on-top, ground-shows-through' path mechanism, which these three wet/soft-ground types require to stay honest over water/bog. Needs declaring as a third G-stack render mode.

Cross-class kerb skeleton sharing: g_path_flagstone_garden and g_path_paved_pebble_setts declare edgeStyle 'both' and depend on the biome-agnostic ~6-piece kerb Wang skeleton owned by the formal STREETS/PLAZA class. That shared skeleton must be authored once and referenced, not duplicated per class -- a coordination dependency to flag so the two classes do not each generate their own kerb corpus.

age / maintenance / wealth remain honestly absent (per the D-stack note) — they would otherwise drive the worn/cracked/swept-vs-littered scalars on every yard; until the chronicle wires building age + a maintenance signal, these affordance scalars derive only from available co-drivers (wetness, heat-role, traffic-from-claim-geometry, biome climate-default).

The water-mill leat/wheel edge and quarry sump want a water_edge / hydrology adjacency that is only partially available — the precise leat and flooded-pit geometry leans on water_edge which exists for shorelines but not for built water-courses.

class: WATER-EDGE & COASTAL — manmade surfaces over, along, and into water (the G-stack ground class bridging land to navigable/standing water: timber walkways, stone quays, ramps, decks, platforms and fords). These surfaces are special among grounds because their fill sits PARTLY OR WHOLLY over the water tile, so the "natural biome that shows through/under" is water itself — the paint pass composites plank/stone OVER the Wang water (and its foam/wave overlay), and the seaward EDGE is a water-meeting edge (piling line / wave-lap fringe), not a dirt/grass fringe. All claim from water_edge (the land/water transition, derivable today from terrain-suitability binary water predicates + the roads-sim where a spine terminates at water) and/or the harbour/dock district. The harbour district.kind is DESIGNED (world-compiler 8-district set) but NOT yet emitted by layout.js — so any surface that needs a true harbour/quay district is flagged NEEDS-DECLARING, while surfaces a lone water-adjacent building or a road-spine-meets-water can justify are AVAILABLE-today.

surfaceTypes.label: Timber boardwalk (raised plank walkway over shallows/marsh)
surfaceTypes.fill: longitudinal weathered timber planks on visible piling joists, ~1-tile run direction following the walkway centreline; gaps between boards let the dark water/foam show through in thin lines; greyed salt-bleached oak, nail-stained at each joist
surfaceTypes.claimSource: water_edge

surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: fill geometry biome-agnostic (planks-on-piles); biomeSkins TINT only: swamp=peat-black damp oak + algae-green underside; beach/ocean/shallow_water=salt-bleached pale grey + barnacle speckle near waterline; river/lake=mid-brown river-oak; taiga/tundra=frost-rimed planks + snow-cover overlay; mystic=faint phosphor between-board glow. No new geometry per biome.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (centre-of-walkway foot-polish lane lighter than edges), moss-joints (algae/moss in the wet board gaps, wetness-driven), puddle-wet (soft-light sheen rises with wetness 0-1 from terrain-suitability — boardwalks are always damp), worn (greyed bleach scalar), snow (cold-biome plank snow-cover overlay). cracks weak (planks splinter not crack — defer to D-stack damage).

tierRecommendation: Sort by formality + claim-readiness, but NONE is deferred — the class ships maximal and complete. Three readiness tiers for SEQUENCING the build (not for dropping any): (1) AVAILABLE-today, pilot-cheapest — surfaces that claim from a water_edge point, a street_spine, or a derived building role with NO new district: timber_boardwalk (the natural pilot — informal fringe, reuses water+foam overlay, ~2 fill tiles, zero kerb), ford_stepping_stones and bridge_deck (both claim from street_spine crossing water — the honest crossing pair, ford for shallow / bridge-deck for spanned), jetty_pier_deck and stone_slipway (project from a single water-edge anchor), watermill_race_walkway and fish_drying_platform (claim from the existing mill / fishery building role + D4 mill seam). (2) NEEDS-DECLARING the harbour district — the working/formal waterfront RUN surfaces that only make sense at district scale: dock_quay_planking, stone_wharf_apron, harbour_steps_landing, pontoon_floating_dock. These are the strongest concrete argument for emitting district.kind='harbour' in layout.js (it is DESIGNED in the world-compiler but not emitted). (3) Corpus reuse keeps cost low: the plank-run fill tile is shared by boardwalk/pier/dock/fish-deck/pontoon (one timber corpus, TINT + edge-profile per surface); the wet-gradient mask is shared by slipway/harbour-steps; the kerb skeleton is shared with the formal-grounds class (wharf/race/bridge-parapet are kerb-profile variants). Edge split: informal water surfaces (boardwalk/pier/ford/pontoon/fish-deck) use a procedural piling+foam FRINGE (zero authored edge tiles); formal ones (wharf/slipway/race/bridge/harbour-steps) use the kerbed Wang coping; dock_quay is the canonical BOTH (built bulkhead kerb on land, foam fringe on water). All composite OVER the water Wang + foam/wave overlay, through GL, never a 2D overlay.
gaps: HARBOUR DISTRICT NOT EMITTED: district.kind='harbour' is fully DESIGNED in the world-compiler (8-district set: docks/warehouses/taverns at waterfront, coastal/river settlements only) but layout.js does NOT emit it today (the PLAN lists residential|craft|market|civic|agricultural as available; harbour is design-only). Until declared, the district-scale surfaces (dock_quay_planking, stone_wharf_apron, harbour_steps_landing, pontoon run) have NO honest claim source beyond a degenerate single-building case. This is the single biggest gap for this class.

WETNESS IS BINARY, NOT SCALAR: terrain-suitability exposes only BINARY water predicates (isWaterTile, buildingTouchesWater, isWaterAdjacent) today — there is NO 0-1 wetness scalar (hydrology.js exists but is unintegrated, per the dressing-manifest audit). Water-edge surfaces lean HARDER on wetness than any other grounds class (the slipway/harbour-steps submergence gradient, the always-damp sheen, the waterline algae band ALL want a 0-1 scalar + a local waterline). Today these render at a climate-default scalar (marine high, desert low); the per-tile wet GRADIENT down a slipway/steps and the exact waterline are honestly approximate until a wetness scalar + waterline are wired.

NO WATERLINE / TIDE / WATER-LEVEL SOURCE: several surfaces (slipway, harbour-steps, pontoon, ford) need to know WHERE the current water surface is to place the submerged-vs-dry band and to seat a floating deck at water level. The sim emits no waterline/tide/level — so the wet-band is placed at a static authored fraction of the surface, not a live water level. Tidal variation and seasonal level change are honestly absent.

NO WAVE / SWELL / FLOW SCALAR for motion: the pontoon's bob, the race's fast-flow amplification, and any deck wash-over want a wave/swell/flow magnitude. The water-wave/foam OVERLAY exists visually (water-wave-overlay.js, _foam knobs) but exposes no per-tile magnitude scalar to the grounds pass. So animated bob = honestly absent (pontoon renders static-correct); race-vs-river flow difference is authored, not sim-derived.

WHERE-A-SPINE-MEETS-WATER not tagged: ford_stepping_stones and bridge_deck claim from a street_spine crossing a water tile. The spines (waypoint polylines tagged street/alley) and binary water predicates BOTH exist, but there is no emitted tag marking 'this spine segment is over/at water → resolve to ford (shallow) or bridge (deep/spanned)'. The grounds pass must compute the intersection itself (spine tile AND water predicate) — derivable today but NOT a pre-declared claim; the shallow-vs-deep fork (ford vs bridge) also needs the shallow_water predicate distinguished from deep water (it exists in terrain-suitability but must be wired into the crossing resolver).

WATERFRONT REGION / QUAY-LINE EXTENT not declared: even with a harbour district kind, the QUAY LINE itself (the continuous waterfront edge a wharf/quay/steps run ALONG) is a declared-region concept (like plazas/squares the PLAN flags as NEEDS-DECLARING). There is no emitted 'this polyline is the quay frontage' region, so a district-scale wharf run cannot follow the true waterfront curve — it would have to be re-derived per-tile from water adjacency. Declaring a waterfront/quay region (sibling to declared_plaza) is the clean fix.

FISHERY / CURING SPECIALIZATION not confirmed: fish_drying_platform claims richest from a fishery/curing building specialization.id (like grain_mill exists for the race walkway). Building roles are 100% derived today, but it is unverified that a fishery/fishmonger/curing-shed specialization is in the assignIdentity() table — if absent, the platform falls back to a generic water_edge boathouse claim (leaner) until that role is declared.

OVER-WATER COMPOSITE / DEPTH-SORT ORDER unspecified for the paint pass: these surfaces are unique in the grounds class by sitting OVER the water tile and its foam/wave overlay (boardwalk/pier/pontoon/ford especially). The chunk-bake paint pass must composite the surface ABOVE the water + foam but still let the foam show in board-gaps / around ford stones / under a pontoon edge, AND depth-sort the raised deck against the player and against the water it floats over. The existing grounds paint-pass design (paint-on-top, before sprites) does not yet specify the water+foam+over-water-deck z-order — a concrete ordering decision is needed before these render correctly through GL (and it must NOT regress into a 2D overlay).

class: MANAGED GREEN & AGRICULTURAL — nature pushed into manmade/ornamental order. Still "grounds" (it overrides natural F0-F8 flora with MANAGED flora + a worked ground plane), so it routes through the SAME G-stack as paved surfaces: a per-tile surface.manmade='<type>' flag + a chunk-bake paint pass compositing the managed-ground fill (+ optional edge) OVER the natural Wang terrain, through GL, never recomputing Wang, never a 2D overlay. The defining twist of this class vs paved grounds: the override is not opaque pavement but a MANAGED-FLORA REGIME — it sets a flora-override channel (managedFlora='<crop|turf|hedge|orchard|grape|bed|grass|topiary>') that (a) SUPPRESSES the natural F0-F8 decoration claim on the tile (reusing the exact roads-sim 'paved' flora-suppression delta mechanism, generalized from 'paved' to 'managed'/'tilled'/'sown'/'mown') and (b) re-seeds a DETERMINISTIC managed pattern keyed on (wx,wy): plough furrow phase, orchard/vineyard row lattice, parterre knot, mown stripe, hedge spine. Edges split by formality exactly like the rest of the engine: formal ornamental surfaces (parterre, topiary court, cemetery lawn, doorstep paving) take the biome-agnostic ~6-piece kerb/edging Wang skeleton (a low box-edging or coping run); working agricultural surfaces (tilled field, orchard, vineyard, pasture) take the procedural FRINGE (feathered crop-stubble/grass-into-wild over the seam, plus fence-line or hedgerow as a separate D5/D6 perimeter prop, NOT an authored ground edge). Biome variation = biomeSkins TINT + climate crop-swap (wheat→rice paddy in tropical/swamp, terraced→narrow in mountains, snow-stubble overlay in arctic), NOT new fill geometry. Affordances ride the ground plane: wear-paths (cart-rut between furrows, mown desire-line across a lawn), puddle-when-wet (flooded paddy, waterlogged furrow), moss-in-joints (cemetery coping), snow-cover (winter-fallow), seasonal phase (sown/green/golden/harvested-stubble/winter-fallow on crops; bloom/bare on parterre). NO-MOCK posture: agricultural & entertainment(garden) & religious DISTRICT WEDGES and building ROLES (healing_order/herbalist herb-garden, stable paddock, grain_mill adjacent field) are AVAILABLE-today as claim regions/anchors; but the sim today places only BUILDINGS inside those wedges — the actual field-plot / orchard-grid / cemetery-plot / declared garden-precinct SUB-REGIONS that this class paints are NOT yet emitted by layout.js and are flagged NEEDS-DECLARING per surface. The doorstep+courtyard surfaces ride the AVAILABLE architectureClaimAt() perimeter ring today.

surfaceTypes.label: Manicured Lawn / Mown Turf
surfaceTypes.fill: Dense even short-cropped grass, deterministic mown-stripe banding (alternating light/dark mow direction keyed on a region-axis projection of wx,wy), no weeds/wildflowers — the natural F1 ground-cover and F2-F3 flora are SUPPRESSED via the managed-flora override and replaced by uniform turf. Reads as deliberately kept ground.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_region (a settlement 'green'/lawn precinct) + district:civic|entertainment|religious wedge interior. Building-adjacent ornamental lawn rides building_role:manor|town_hall|monastery via perimeter ring.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (the lawn/green precinct sub-region is not emitted by layout.js; the entertainment-garden & civic district WEDGE that would contain it IS available-today, and the perimeter-ring lawn around a manor/civic building is available-today via architectureClaimAt). Mown-stripe pattern is pure f(wx,wy), fully deterministic now.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Grassland/temperate = vivid kept-green. Drier biomes (savanna/steppe) tint the turf yellow-green and shorten the stripe contrast (struggling lawn). Tropical = lusher saturated green. Arctic/tundra/taiga = the formal lawn is honestly rare; render as a hardy moss-turf and apply the snow-cover affordance most of the year. Mystic = faint luminous blue-green sheen. Geometry (stripe lattice + edging) is biome-agnostic; only tint + a climate viability bias changes.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (mown desire-line / footpath worn diagonally across the turf where traffic cuts the corner — keyed on nearest spine), puddle-wet (shallow sheen in low spots when wet), snow-cover (winter), moss-joints (only at the kerb edging seam). Seasonal: greener in growing season, strawer in drought/dormancy.
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 turf fill tile + the shared 6-piece biome-agnostic kerb/edging Wang skeleton (reused, low box-edging skin) for the formal lawn-edge; informal lawn-into-meadow uses the procedural fringe instead. Native 32px. Mown stripes are procedural, not authored. ~7 shared pieces, no per-biome geometry.
surfaceTypes.notes: Pure managed-flora override: the load-bearing thing is SUPPRESSING natural flora + painting uniform turf, mirroring the roads-sim 'paved' suppression but with managedFlora='turf' rather than an opaque paver. Distinct from natural grassland (which keeps its wild F1-F3 scatter).

surfaceTypes.label: Formal Garden Parterre / Knot Garden
surfaceTypes.fill: Geometric ornamental beds: clipped low-hedge (box) outlines enclosing coloured infill (gravel paths between, bedding-flower blocks, coloured earth). A deterministic knot/scrollwork lattice keyed on the precinct's local axes so the pattern is coherent across many tiles, not per-tile noise. The most heavily 'ordered nature' surface in the class.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_plaza|declared_region (an ornamental garden precinct) inside a district:entertainment (anchor 'garden') wedge or building_role:manor|palace|monastery|town_hall forecourt.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (the garden precinct polygon must be declared in layout.js — today only the entertainment district WEDGE and the 'garden' anchor BUILDING exist, not the laid-out parterre region around it). The knot lattice is deterministic f(wx,wy + precinct axes) once the region is declared.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = box-hedge + bright bedding flowers. Desert/savanna = a xeric formal garden: gravel-dominant with succulent/agave bedding blocks, hedge swapped to drought shrub. Tropical = denser, broad-leaf ornamental infill. Arctic/tundra = render as a gravel-and-evergreen formal court (flower beds honestly absent most of year, snow-cover overlay). Mystic = glowing ornamental infill. Hedge/gravel/bed geometry biome-agnostic; infill palette + plant species via tint+climate swap.
surfaceTypes.affordances: moss-joints (between the path gravel and the hedge kerb), puddle-wet (gravel paths pool slightly), wear-paths (gravel scuffs along the main axis), snow-cover, seasonal bloom (beds go bare→bud→bloom→spent; hedge stays evergreen). Maintenance is honestly-absent so default to KEPT (no overgrowth) until a maintenance source exists.
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 gravel-path fill + 1 bedding-infill fill + the shared 6-piece kerb skeleton skinned as a clipped low-hedge edging (this is the marquee use of the formal kerb Wang). Hedge corners reuse the outer/inner-corner pieces. ~8 shared pieces + procedural knot lattice. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: The clipped-hedge edging IS the kerb Wang skeleton wearing a green skin — proves the kerb corpus is biome-and-material-agnostic (cobble kerb vs box hedge are the same 6 masks). Heaviest 'nature forced into manmade order' exemplar.

surfaceTypes.label: Hedge-Lined Walk / Allée
surfaceTypes.fill: A kept walking surface (fine gravel, raked earth, or stepping-stone-in-turf) running as a linear corridor, flanked on BOTH sides by a continuous clipped hedge or pleached-tree allée. The fill is the path; the hedge is the defining ornamental flora-override band on the verge tiles.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: street_spine|alley_spine (the AVAILABLE waypoint polyline) given a DECLARED planted-verge offset, OR a declared_region promenade inside district:entertainment|civic.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING for the verge planting (the spine polyline IS available-today and the walk surface can be claimed off it now, but the decision to plant a hedge allée on a given spine — vs leave it a plain alley — is a declared upgrade). The procedural row-spacing of the hedge/allée trees is deterministic f(distance-along-spine).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = box/yew hedge or pleached lime. Mediterranean/savanna = cypress allée. Tropical = palm or bamboo allée. Arctic/taiga = clipped conifer hedge (hardy). Desert = the allée degrades to spaced shade-trees rather than a continuous hedge (climate honesty). Mystic = luminous topiary allée. Path fill + hedge-band geometry biome-agnostic; species via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (centre of the walk wears to bare earth), puddle-wet (gravel pools), moss-joints (stepping-stone joints + hedge-base), snow-cover, seasonal (deciduous allée goes bare in winter; evergreen hedge persists). Shade affordance: the allée casts a managed-shade band useful to D2 moss growth.
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 walk fill (shared with garden gravel) + the shared kerb skeleton as a low hedge-base edging on each verge + D5/D6 perimeter hedge/tree props for the actual vertical hedge body (the hedge VOLUME is a prop, the ground-band is the surface). ~6 shared edge pieces. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Bridges the spine (AVAILABLE) and the declared-verge (NEEDS-DECLARING). The hedge as a tall body is a perimeter prop (D6-style), but its FOOTPRINT band is a managed-green ground surface that suppresses natural flora — that footprint is what this entry paints.

surfaceTypes.label: Topiary Court / Ornamental Shrubbery Ground
surfaceTypes.fill: Kept ground (clipped turf or gravel) hosting a deterministic GRID of topiary-shrub footprints — the ground-plane signature is the regular shrub-pad lattice + the kept surface between, distinct from a parterre's flat knot-beds by being a sparse 3D-shrub court.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: declared_region inside district:entertainment (anchor 'garden') or building_role:manor|palace|monastery ornamental court.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (topiary court precinct not emitted; entertainment-garden district wedge available-today as the container). Shrub-pad lattice is deterministic f(wx,wy + court axes).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = box/yew topiary on turf. Desert = sculpted-succulent court on gravel. Tropical = sculpted broadleaf. Arctic = sculpted dwarf-conifer on gravel, snow-cover dominant. Mystic = glowing topiary. The ground surface + pad-lattice geometry biome-agnostic; the shrub species (a D6 prop) skins per biome.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (visitors weave between pads → desire-lines), moss-joints (gravel/kerb seams), puddle-wet, snow-cover, seasonal (evergreen topiary persists; turf greens/strawes). Maintenance honestly-absent → default kept-sharp.
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: Shares the lawn turf fill + garden gravel fill + the shared kerb skeleton edging; the topiary shrubs themselves are D6 perimeter-scatter props placed on the lattice. ~6 shared edge pieces, 0 new fill geometry. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Mostly a placement pattern (shrub lattice) over the lawn/gravel fills already defined — the NEW thing here is the deterministic court lattice + flora-override that swaps natural flora for sculpted shrubs. Listed separately because its claim source and affordance (weave-between desire-lines) differ from flat parterre.

surfaceTypes.label: Tilled / Furrowed Crop Field
surfaceTypes.fill: Ploughed earth in deterministic parallel FURROWS (ridge-and-furrow), the furrow axis coherent across the whole plot (keyed on the plot's declared long-axis, not per-tile noise). Carries a SEASONAL crop-phase channel: bare-tilled / sown / green-shoots / tall-green / golden-ripe / harvested-stubble / winter-fallow. Natural flora fully SUPPRESSED (this is the canonical 'managed flora overrides natural flora' surface) — managedFlora='crop', tilled-suppression delta directly analogous to the roads 'paved' delta.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:agricultural (anchor 'barn') wedge interior — AVAILABLE-today as the wedge — but the per-plot FIELD region + its long-axis is declared. Also building_role:grain_mill|farmstead adjacency.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (layout.js places barns inside the agricultural wedge but emits NO field-plot regions; the wedge IS available-today as a coarse container/claim-source, the tilled sub-plots with furrow axis + crop assignment are the declared part). Furrow phase + crop pattern are deterministic f(wx,wy + plot axis) once declared.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Grassland/temperate = wheat/barley/rye, brown loam furrows. Tropical/swamp/river = RICE PADDY climate-swap: furrows become flooded bunded paddies (puddle-wet affordance permanently on, water sheen), managedFlora='paddy'. Savanna/steppe = sorghum/millet, paler dust-soil. Desert = irrigated plot only near water (honestly sparse), pale alluvial soil. Mountains/hills = TERRACED narrow contour furrows (row geometry follows slope contours). Arctic/tundra = honestly absent / hardy-root stubble with snow-cover most of year. Furrow-lattice geometry biome-agnostic (re-axised for terraces/paddies); soil tint + crop species via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (cart-rut headland track around the plot edge + plough-turn scuffs), puddle-wet (waterlogged furrows after rain; permanent for paddy), mud/worn (bare-tilled phase is all mud), snow-cover (winter-fallow), seasonal crop-phase (the dominant affordance — drives the whole look across the year).
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 tilled-soil fill carrying procedural furrow direction + 1 crop-overlay fill per phase (procedural row of crop sprites/texture, phase-indexed) — fill regenerates via tint/phase, NOT new geometry per crop. Edges = procedural fringe (crop thins into wild grass/hedgerow at the plot margin) + a fence-line/hedgerow as a D6 perimeter prop. Native 32px fill. NO authored kerb (working land).
surfaceTypes.notes: THE exemplar of the class's defining mechanic: managed flora overriding natural flora using the generalized 'paved'→'tilled' suppression delta. Crop-phase is the richest seasonal affordance in the whole grounds engine. Fence/hedgerow border is a prop, not a ground edge — correctly fringe-edged.

surfaceTypes.label: Orchard Rows (Managed Tree Grid)
surfaceTypes.fill: A kept GROUND between regularly-gridded fruit/nut trees: mown or grazed grass alleys + bare-earth tree circles, with a deterministic square/quincunx tree lattice keyed on the orchard's declared origin+spacing. The ground surface is the managed grass-alley + tree-base discs; the trees are D6 props standing on the lattice. managedFlora='orchard' suppresses wild scatter, keeps the alley grass mown.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:agricultural wedge (AVAILABLE container) + declared orchard plot, OR building_role:olive_press|farmstead|cidery adjacency (e.g. olive_press specialization implies olive groves).
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (orchard plot region + tree-grid spacing declared; agricultural district wedge available-today as container; olive_press building role is an available no-mock HINT that an orchard belongs nearby). Lattice deterministic f(wx,wy + orchard origin).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = apple/pear/cherry, green mown alleys. Mediterranean/savanna = OLIVE grove (ties to olive_press role), silver-green, dry pale grass alleys. Tropical = citrus/mango, lush alleys. Hills = terraced orchard following contours. Cold (taiga) = hardy fruit/nut. Arctic = honestly absent. Lattice + alley-ground geometry biome-agnostic; tree species (D6 prop) + alley-grass tint via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (cart track down the main alley + ladder/picking scuffs at tree bases), puddle-wet (alley low spots), moss-joints (tree-base damp rings), snow-cover, seasonal (blossom→fruit→leaf-fall→bare, on the prop trees; alley grass greens/strawes; windfall litter in autumn as D6 ground prop).
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: Reuses the lawn/mown-grass fill for the alley + a bare-earth tree-disc decal at each lattice node; trees are D6 perimeter/scatter props on the grid. Procedural fringe at the orchard margin. ~0 new fill geometry (composes lawn fill + disc decal + grid). Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Ground-plane is mostly the managed mown alley + tree discs; the orchard's identity comes from the deterministic tree LATTICE this surface paints + the flora-override. olive_press is a genuine available no-mock signal linking a building role to this surface.

surfaceTypes.label: Vineyard Rows (Trellised Vines)
surfaceTypes.fill: Long parallel TRELLIS rows of trained grapevines with worked bare/cover-crop earth between — a tight linear lattice (closer-spaced than orchard, with a strong single row-axis) keyed on the vineyard's declared slope-aligned axis. Ground = the inter-row worked strip; vines+trellis are D6 props on the row-lines. managedFlora='grape'.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:agricultural wedge (AVAILABLE container) + declared vineyard plot, OR building_role:vintner|winery adjacency. Strong slope/aspect preference (south-facing hillsides).
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (vineyard plot + row axis declared; agricultural wedge available-today; a vintner/winery building role would be an available hint — note vineyard is not yet a distinct specialization, closest is feast_hall/olive_press, so the role hint is weaker than orchard). Row pattern deterministic f(wx,wy + axis).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Mediterranean/grassland/hills = classic terraced or contour grape rows, dry worked soil. Tropical = honestly rare (swap to a tropical-vine cover crop or drop). Cold (taiga/tundra) = honestly absent. Desert = only irrigated near water. Mountains/hills = TERRACED contour rows (the canonical vineyard look). Row geometry biome-agnostic (re-axised for terraces); soil tint + vine state via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (worker track along each row-end headland), puddle-wet (inter-row low spots), seasonal (bare-cane winter → bud → leaf → green-grape → ripe-purple → harvested → leaf-fall, on the vine props), snow-cover (winter dormancy), mud/worn (bare worked inter-row strips).
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 worked-inter-row earth fill (can share the tilled-soil fill with a finer skin) + D6 trellis/vine props on the row-lines. Procedural fringe margin. ~0 new fill geometry. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Distinct from orchard by tighter linear single-axis rows + trellis props + strong slope/aspect bias. Role hint weaker (no dedicated vintner specialization today) so claim leans more on the agricultural district wedge + declared plot.

surfaceTypes.label: Raised-Bed / Kitchen Garden (Potager)
surfaceTypes.fill: A small intensively-worked garden of rectangular RAISED BEDS separated by narrow trodden-earth or board paths — a fine deterministic bed-grid (much smaller cell than a field) of mixed vegetables/herbs. Sits tight against dwellings. managedFlora='bed'. Mixed-planting look (not monoculture rows).
surfaceTypes.claimSource: building_role:cottage|farmstead|healing_order|herbalist|herbseller PERIMETER (rides the AVAILABLE architectureClaimAt ring 1-3 behind/beside the dwelling), and district:agricultural|residential edges. healing_order ('herb gardens') & herbalist & herbseller are AVAILABLE no-mock role hints that this surface belongs adjacent.
surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today for the perimeter-ring placement (architectureClaimAt exists; healing_order/herbalist/herbseller specialization.id are available no-mock anchors). NEEDS-DECLARING only for the precise bed layout polygon if larger than the ring. Bed-grid deterministic f(wx,wy + building origin).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = mixed veg/herb beds, dark worked soil, optional board-edging. Desert = sunken beds (water-saving) with shade. Tropical = lush dense beds. Arctic/tundra = cold-frame / hardy-root beds, snow-cover-protected, small. Mystic = glowing herb beds (esp. for healing_order). Bed-grid + edging geometry biome-agnostic; planting palette via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (worn tending-paths between beds), puddle-wet (path low spots, bed over-watering sheen), mud/worn (bare beds between plantings), moss-joints (board/stone bed edging), snow-cover, seasonal (continuous succession-planting — patchier phase than a monoculture field).
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: 1 worked-bed fill (fine soil + mixed-crop overlay) + optional shared kerb skeleton as a low board/stone bed-edging (the 'both' edge style: edged if formal kitchen garden, fringe if rustic) + narrow path fill (shared with garden gravel). ~6 shared edge pieces optional. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: The most AVAILABLE-today surface in the class: it legitimately rides the existing perimeter ring + three existing herb/healing role anchors, needing no new region declaration. Strong no-mock grounding — healing_order's desc literally says 'herb gardens'.

surfaceTypes.label: Threshold Doorstep Paving + Courtyard Garden
surfaceTypes.fill: A composite micro-surface immediately at a dwelling's door: a paved/flagged DOORSTEP + path stub, transitioning to a small enclosed COURTYARD garden (kept turf, a few beds, a tree, pot plants). Blends a hard paved threshold (formal kerb-edged) with a soft managed-green courtyard (fringe or low edging). Rides the building perimeter directly.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: building_role:ANY dwelling/courthouse/manor — anchored on the AVAILABLE architectureClaimAt perimeter ring + the door SOCKET (door_path approach). The threshold sits on ring 0-1 at the door; the courtyard fills an enclosed perimeter pocket.
surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today (architectureClaimAt + the door socket/door_path are available no-mock anchors; this is the D5 ground-landscaping perimeter precedent applied to managed green). NEEDS-DECLARING only for a fully enclosed courtyard polygon on larger buildings. Deterministic per-tile off the building origin + door position.
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = flagstone doorstep + turf courtyard. Desert = packed-earth threshold + shaded gravel court with potted succulents. Tropical = stone step + lush potted court. Arctic = timber doorstep + snow-cleared swept stub, minimal green. Mystic = glowing threshold runes (tint only). The paving + edging geometry biome-agnostic; courtyard planting + threshold material via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (heavy worn track at the threshold — the single most-trodden tile in the settlement; swept-clear band), puddle-wet (doorstep pooling), moss-joints (flag joints + courtyard kerb), snow-cover (but threshold often swept), seasonal (potted plants + courtyard turf cycle).
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: Reuses a paved flagstone fill (shared with the broader paved-grounds class) for the threshold + the shared kerb skeleton for the doorstep edge + lawn/bed fills for the courtyard. ~6 shared edge pieces, 0 new fill. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: A deliberate HYBRID with the paved-grounds class at the doorstep, going managed-green in the courtyard — demonstrates the kerb Wang + fringe coexisting on one micro-surface. Fully AVAILABLE-today via the perimeter ring + door socket; the richest no-mock anchor (every building has a door).

surfaceTypes.label: Fenced Managed Pasture / Paddock
surfaceTypes.fill: Enclosed GRAZED grassland — kept shorter and patchier than wild meadow (cropped by livestock), with deterministic graze-patches, dung scatter, bare poached patches near gates/water, and well-trodden stock-paths. Bounded by a fence or dry-stone wall (D6 perimeter prop). managedFlora='pasture' (lighter override than crops — it's still grass, just managed/grazed).
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:agricultural wedge (AVAILABLE container) + declared paddock, AND building_role:riding_stable|draft_stable|breeding_stable|farrier_shop|farmstead adjacency — the STABLE specializations are AVAILABLE no-mock hints that a paddock belongs beside them.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING for the paddock polygon (the agricultural wedge + the four stable specialization.ids are available-today as anchors/hints; the fenced enclosure region itself is declared). Graze-patch + poach pattern deterministic f(wx,wy).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = green grazed turf, dry-stone or post-rail fence. Savanna/steppe = open dry rangeland, sparser graze. Tropical = lush paddock. Mountains/hills = stone-walled hill pasture (transhumance). Arctic/tundra = hardy reindeer/sheep pasture, snow-cover dominant, lichen-graze. Desert = sparse near-water paddock only. Graze-pattern geometry biome-agnostic; grass tint + fence material via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (stock-paths converging on gate + water trough; poached-mud bare patches), puddle-wet (trampled wet hollows, trough overflow), mud/worn (gate poaching is permanent mud), snow-cover, moss-joints (at stone-wall base), seasonal (lush spring → grazed-down summer → muddy winter).
surfaceTypes.assetCorpus: Reuses the lawn/turf fill with a patchier grazed skin + poach-mud decals; fence/wall is a D6 perimeter prop (not a ground edge → procedural fringe at the grass margin). Water trough is a D6 prop. ~0 new fill geometry. Native 32px.
surfaceTypes.notes: Lightest flora-override in the class (still grass, just grazed/managed) — sits between wild meadow and tilled field. Strong AVAILABLE no-mock role grounding via the four stable specializations. Fence is correctly a prop, so the surface is fringe-edged.

surfaceTypes.label: Cemetery / Churchyard Lawn
surfaceTypes.fill: A solemn KEPT lawn (or gravel-and-turf) hosting a deterministic GRID of grave plots — mown grass between, with grave-mound discs / headstone bases / cross sockets on the lattice. Quieter, more uniform than a parterre; the order is funereal not ornamental. managedFlora='grass' + grave-lattice. Headstones are D6 props on the grid.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:religious (anchor monastery|temple|chapel) wedge — AVAILABLE container — + a DECLARED churchyard/cemetery region beside the religious building (building_role:chapel|monastery|temple).
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING (no graveyard region is emitted; the religious district wedge + the chapel/monastery/temple building roles ARE available-today as anchors). Grave-grid lattice deterministic f(wx,wy + churchyard origin).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = mown grass + weathered headstones + yew trees. Desert = gravel cemetery with above-ground tombs, no turf. Tropical = lush overgrown-tending churchyard. Arctic/tundra = snow-covered cairns/markers, hardy turf. Mountains = terraced graveyard. Mystic = faintly glowing markers (tint). Lawn + grave-lattice + low coping-wall geometry biome-agnostic; markers (D6 props) + turf/gravel via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (mourner desire-lines between rows + to the gate/church door), moss-joints (HEAVY — moss on coping walls + headstone bases + path joints; this surface leans into moss-in-joints more than any other), puddle-wet, snow-cover, seasonal (laid flowers as D6 props, autumn leaf-litter). Age/neglect honestly-absent → default kept (no overgrowth) until maintenance source exists.

Combines the parterre's order with the kitchen-garden's utility. managedFlora='bed'+'turf'. Strong cross-axial quartered geometry.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: building_role:monastery|healing_order (AVAILABLE — healing_order's desc literally 'herb gardens') + district:religious wedge. The enclosing building's courtyard footprint defines the garth.
surfaceTypes.available: AVAILABLE-today as anchors (healing_order + monastery building roles + religious district wedge all exist; healing_order is an explicit no-mock 'herb garden' hint), NEEDS-DECLARING only for the precise enclosed-garth polygon. Quartered-path lattice deterministic f(wx,wy + garth centre).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Temperate = lawn garth + herb beds + central well/fountain (D6 prop). Desert = a shaded courtyard with a central water channel, gravel + potted herbs. Tropical = lush physic garden. Arctic = small cloistered cold-frame herb garden. Mystic = glowing medicinal herbs (esp. healing_order). Garth geometry (quartered cross + edging) biome-agnostic; herb palette + central feature via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (cross-path wear, well-approach), moss-joints (cloister coping + path joints — damp shaded courtyard favours moss), puddle-wet, snow-cover, seasonal (herb beds cycle; lawn garth persists). Shade affordance high (enclosed by building) → favours D2 moss/fern growth.

surfaceTypes.notes: Combines lawn + bed + path fills already defined into a quartered cloister pattern — the new thing is the cross-axial garth geometry + the strong AVAILABLE healing_order/monastery no-mock anchor (one of the best role-to-surface links in the class).

surfaceTypes.label: Managed Hay Meadow / Mowing Ground
surfaceTypes.fill: A managed (not wild) hay meadow: tall uniform mowing-grass that is CUT seasonally — its signature is the seasonal phase (tall green → flowering hay → MOWN-IN-SWATHES with deterministic windrow lines + drying haycocks → stubble → regrowth). Less wild than natural meadow (fewer weeds, kept for fodder). managedFlora='hay'. Ties to the existing hay_bales D6 prop.
surfaceTypes.claimSource: district:agricultural wedge (AVAILABLE container) + declared meadow plot; building_role:farmstead|draft_stable|barn adjacency (fodder for livestock). The existing D6 hay_bales object (only:[grassland,savanna,steppe,hills,river,lake,forest]) is an available no-mock signal that hay-making happens in those biomes.
surfaceTypes.available: NEEDS-DECLARING for the meadow plot (agricultural wedge available-today; hay_bales D6 biome-restriction list is an available no-mock hint for WHERE hay meadows belong). Windrow/swathe pattern deterministic f(wx,wy + mow axis + season).
surfaceTypes.biomeSkins: Restricted (mirrors hay_bales) to grassland/savanna/steppe/hills/river/lake/forest as primary; rice-straw analog in tropical paddy regions; honestly absent in desert/arctic/ocean. Temperate = lush hay; steppe/savanna = drier, sparser. Windrow geometry biome-agnostic; grass tint + cut-timing via skin.
surfaceTypes.affordances: wear-paths (mowing-machine/scythe passes + cart track to collect cocks), puddle-wet, snow-cover (winter dormancy), seasonal (the DOMINANT affordance — uncut→flowering→swathed-windrows→haycocks→stubble→regrowth, with D6 hay_bales/haycock props appearing at the swathe stage), mud/worn (gateways).
